admitted_candidate_cards.proof_strategy: Count incident edge-ends: every edge contributes exactly two ends in a loopless undirected simple graph.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a finite simple undirected graph G.
incidence: Count all incidences by summing degree(G,v) over vertices.
edge-view: Each edge supplies exactly two incidences because G is loopless and undirected.
equate: The two finite counts are equal.
conclude: degree_sum(G) = nat_mul(2, edge_count(G)).

lean.target:
∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
    (∑ v, G.degree v) = 2 * G.edgeFinset.card
lean.witness:
example : ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
    (∑ v, G.degree v) = 2 * G.edgeFinset.card := by
  intro V _ G _
  exact G.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges

admitted_candidate_cards.proof_strategy: Use the finite-tree cardinality theorem after fixing the profile convention that tree means connected and acyclic.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix G and assume tree(G).
model: Unpack tree as connected and acyclic in the finite simple graph model.
finite-count: Apply the finite-tree edge-cardinality theorem.
normalize: Identify edge_count(G) and vertex_count(G) with the two finite cardinalities.
conclude: nat_add(edge_count(G),1) = vertex_count(G).

lean.target:
∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
    G.IsTree → G.edgeFinset.card + 1 = Fintype.card V
lean.witness:
example : ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
    G.IsTree → G.edgeFinset.card + 1 = Fintype.card V := by
  intro V _ _ G _ hG
  exact hG.card_edgeFinset

root: Choose a root using connectedness.
color: Color each vertex by the parity of its graph distance from the root.
separate: Adjacent vertices have distances differing by one in a tree.
conclude: The parity coloring witnesses bipartite(G).

admitted_candidate_cards.proof_strategy: Pair entrance and exit incidences along an Euler trail; only its endpoints can contribute unpaired incidences.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix G and a trail t with is_euler_trail(G,t).
coverage: Every edge occurs exactly once in t.
internal-pairing: Each internal visit pairs one entering and one leaving incidence.
endpoints: Only the two trail endpoints may have unpaired incidences.
parity: Therefore all degrees are even except possibly two endpoint degrees.
conclude: odd_degree_count(G) is 0 or 2.

lean.target:
∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    {u v : V} (p : G.Walk u v), p.IsEulerian →
      Fintype.card {w | Odd (G.degree w)} = 0 ∨ Fintype.card {w | Odd (G.degree w)} = 2
lean.witness:
example : ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    {u v : V} (p : G.Walk u v), p.IsEulerian →
      Fintype.card {w | Odd (G.degree w)} = 0 ∨ Fintype.card {w | Odd (G.degree w)} = 2 := by
  intro V _ _ G _ u v p hp
  exact hp.card_odd_degree

excluded_witnesses.canonical_statement: A finite graph has an Euler trail if and only if its non-isolated vertices are connected and it has zero or two odd-degree vertices.
excluded_witnesses.reason: The pinned Trails module supplies the necessary `Walk.IsEulerian.card_odd_degree` theorem but leaves the relevant existence direction as TODO. The design therefore marks GRAF-006 blocked; no proof receipt or XML card may claim the converse.
excluded_witnesses.required_evidence: Compile a constructive existence theorem against the exact nonisolated_connected convention, including the zero-edge case, then add an independently reviewed Trail(G) lowering receipt.

excluded_witnesses.canonical_statement: A finite graph is bipartite if and only if it has a proper bipartition L,R covering every vertex.
excluded_witnesses.reason: `SimpleGraph.isBipartite_iff_exists_isBipartiteWith` is close, but its sets need not cover isolated vertices. The profile predicate proper_bipartition requires total coverage, so this is not a three-way exact statement yet.
excluded_witnesses.required_evidence: Prove and compile a bridge that extends a mathlib bipartition over isolated vertices while preserving the exact VertexClass(G) semantics, then obtain independent review.
